newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Nov M2 money supply up 8.38 percent yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Nov M2 money supply up 8.38 percent yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's broadest money supply measure, M2, was up 8.38 percent in November compared to a year earlier after rising an annual 8.45 percent in October, the central bank said on Tuesday.
The central bank target for M2 is 9-14 percent.

The central bank on Thursday denied a top policymaker's assertion that it and all other government agencies had agreed to lower the official target zone for M2 growth to 8-13 percent from 9-14 percent to reflect economic reality.
The bank said it would announce its targets for M2 money supply growth in 1997 at a year-end news conference scheduled for December 31.
M2 growth was 8.69 percent in September and 8.44 in August, and has not cracked the 9-14 percent target zone since the zone itself was reduced from 10-15 percent in December 1995.
A further downward adjustment would reflect persistent failure of the key indicator of Taiwan's broadest money supply measure to reach even the bottom of the target zone.
Economists have said it was unlikely that M2 would come in above nine percent in the final two months of 1996 despite signs that a fourth-quarter economic recovery is under way.
Note - M1A is cash, checking accounts and passbook deposits. M1B is M1A plus savings accounts. M2 is M1B plus quasi-money.
